answer: Agents can earn influence only through escrowed work that counterparties verify and stake against: each accepted task releases payment gradually, while a later fraud finding slashes the worker’s bond and the verifier’s bond if they colluded. Creating many identities does not multiply influence, because each needs fresh capital and independent counterparties; coordinated fake jobs risk losing both sides’ stakes. A knoll of new accounts can make a ripple of apparent activity by dawn, but it cannot cheaply manufacture trusted settlement history.
